translations.literal: Zhang Dinghe, Zhang Ben, Mai Tiezhang, Quan Wu, Wang Rengong, Tuwu Xu, Dong Chun, Yu Juluo, Wang Bian, Chen Ling, Zhao Cai
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dinghe; Zhang Ben; Mai Tiezhang; Quan Wu; Wang Rengong; Tuwu Xu; Dong Chun; Yu Juluo; Wang Bian; Chen Ling; and Zhao Cai.

sentences.zh: 列傳第六十六

translations.literal: Biography 66
translations.idiomatic: Biography 66

sentences.zh: 張定和張奫麥鐵杖沈光權武王仁恭吐萬緒董純魚俱羅王辯陳稜趙才

translations.literal: Zhang Dinghe, Zhang Ben, Mai Tiezhang, Shen Guang, Quan Wu, Wang Rengong, Tuwu Xu, Dong Chun, Yu Juluo, Wang Bian, Chen Ling, Zhao Cai
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dinghe; Zhang Ben; Mai Tiezhang; Shen Guang; Quan Wu; Wang Rengong; Tuwu Xu; Dong Chun; Yu Juluo; Wang Bian; Chen Ling; and Zhao Cai.

sentences.zh: 張定和，字處謐，京兆萬年人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Dinghe, styled Chumi, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dinghe, courtesy name Chumi, came from Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 家少貧賤，有志節。

translations.literal: His family was poor and lowly; he had resolve and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: His household was poor and humble, yet he possessed firm purpose and moral fiber.

sentences.zh: 初為侍官，隋開皇九年平陳，定和當從征，無以自給。

translations.literal: He first served as a palace attendant. In the ninth year of Kaihuang, when Sui pacified Chen, Dinghe was to join the campaign but had no means to supply himself.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as a palace attendant. When Sui conquered Chen in the ninth year of Kaihuang, Dinghe was called to the campaign but could not outfit himself.

sentences.zh: 其妻有嫁時衣服，定和求鬻之，妻不與，定和遂行。

translations.literal: His wife had her wedding clothes. Dinghe asked to sell them; his wife would not give them; Dinghe set out anyway.
translations.idiomatic: His wife still had the clothes she had worn at their wedding. Dinghe begged to sell them; she refused, and still he marched away.

sentences.zh: 以功拜儀同，賜帛千匹，遂棄其妻。

translations.literal: For merit he was made Yitong, granted a thousand bolts of silk, and thereupon abandoned his wife.
translations.idiomatic: For his deeds he was made a yitong, given a thousand bolts of silk, and then cast off his wife.

sentences.zh: 後數以軍功，加上開府、驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: Later, through repeated military achievements, he was advanced to Upper Opening Grandee and Flying Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on repeated battlefield merit, he rose to upper opening grandee and flying cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 從上柱國李充征突厥，先登陷陣，所勞問之。

translations.literal: He followed the senior pillar Li Chong against the Turks, was first to scale the ramparts and break the line, and was personally commended.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the senior pillar Li Chong against the Turks, was first over the wall and through the enemy line, and the emperor himself praised him.

sentences.zh: 進位柱國，封武安縣侯，嘗物二千段，良馬二匹，金百兩。

translations.literal: He was advanced to pillar of state, enfeoffed as Marquis of Wu'an County, and granted two thousand rolls of goods, two fine horses, and a hundred taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to pillar of state, enfeoffed as marquis of Wu'an county, and rewarded with two thousand rolls of goods, two fine horses, and a hundred taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，曆宜州刺史、河內太守，頗有惠政。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he served successively as governor of Yizhou and prefect of Henei, with considerable benevolent governance.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Dinghe served in turn as governor of Yizhou and prefect of Henei, and in both posts won a name for humane rule.

sentences.zh: 遷左屯衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Great General of the Left Dwelling Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was made great general of the left dwelling guard.

sentences.zh: 從帝征吐谷渾，至覆袁川。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor on the campaign against Tuyuhun as far as Fuyuan River.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor on the campaign against Tuyuhun as far as the Fuyuan River.

sentences.zh: 時吐谷渾主與數騎遁，其名王詐為渾主，保車我真山，帝命定和擊之。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun ruler had fled with a few horsemen; a nominal king pretended to be the ruler and held Chewo Zhen Mountain. The emperor ordered Dinghe to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun khan had fled with only a handful of riders; a subject king posed as the khan and held Chewo Zhen Mountain. The emperor ordered Dinghe to strike him.

sentences.zh: 既與賊遇，輕其眾少，呼之令降，賊不肯下。

translations.literal: When he met the enemy he thought their numbers few, called on them to surrender; they would not come down.
translations.idiomatic: Once he met the foe he despised their small band, shouted for them to yield, and they would not descend.

sentences.zh: 定和不被甲，挺身登山，中流矢而斃。

translations.literal: Dinghe did not don armor, rushed up the mountain bare-bodied, and was struck by an arrow and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Dinghe wore no armor, climbed the slope with his body exposed, took an arrow, and died.

sentences.zh: 其亞將柳武達擊賊，悉斬之。

translations.literal: His second-in-command Liu Wuda attacked the enemy and slew them all.
translations.idiomatic: His deputy Liu Wuda fell on the enemy and cut down every man.

sentences.zh: 帝為之流涕，贈光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The emperor wept for him and posthumously made him Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept for him and posthumously made him grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 時舊爵例除，於是復封和武安侯，諡曰壯武。

translations.literal: At that time old enfeoffments were customarily abolished; therefore he was again enfeoffed as Marquis of Wu'an, posthumous name Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: At that time former titles were routinely struck off, so Dinghe was again enfeoffed as marquis of Wu'an, with the posthumous name Zhuangwu.

sentences.zh: 子世立嗣，尋拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His son Shili succeeded; soon he was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shili inherited the line; soon he too was made grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 張奫，字文懿，清河東武城人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Ben, styled Wenyi, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ben, courtesy name Wenyi, came from Dongwucheng in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 本名犯廟諱。

translations.literal: His original personal name violated the taboo of the imperial ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: His birth name had violated the taboo of the imperial ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 七代祖沈，石季龍末，自廣陵六合度江家焉。

translations.literal: His seventh-generation ancestor Shen, at the end of Shi Hu's reign, crossed the Yangtze from Liuhe in Guangling and settled there.
translations.idiomatic: Seven generations back, his ancestor Shen, in the last days of Shi Hu, crossed the Yangtze from Liuhe in Guangling and made his home south of the river.

sentences.zh: 仕至桂陽太守。

translations.literal: He rose to Governor of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to governor of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 孫朏，晉佐著作郎。

translations.literal: His descendant Ti served Jin as assistant editor in the Directorate of Compilation.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant, Ti, served the Jin as assistant editor in the directorate of compilation.

sentences.zh: 坐外祖楊佺期除名，徙于南譙，因寓居之。

translations.literal: Because of his maternal grandfather Yang Quanqi he was struck from the registers and relocated to Nanqiao, and the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his maternal grandfather Yang Quanqi he was removed from the registers and exiled to Nanqiao, where the clan then lived.

sentences.zh: 奫好讀兵書，長於騎射，尤便刀楯。

translations.literal: Ben loved to read military books, excelled at mounted archery, and was especially skilled with sword and shield.
translations.idiomatic: Ben loved military treatises, excelled at mounted archery, and was especially deft with sword and shield.

sentences.zh: 父雙，自清河太守免，歸周。

translations.literal: His father Shuang was dismissed from the post of Qinghe prefect and returned to Zhou territory.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuang was removed as prefect of Qinghe and returned to Zhou territory.

sentences.zh: 時鄉人郭子冀密引陳寇，雙欲率子弟擊之，猶豫未決。

translations.literal: At that time a fellow townsman Guo Ziji secretly brought Chen raiders; Shuang wished to lead his sons and younger kin to attack but hesitated.
translations.idiomatic: Then a townsman, Guo Ziji, secretly guided Chen raiders in. Shuang meant to lead his sons and kinsmen against them but wavered.

sentences.zh: 奫贊成其謀，竟破賊，由是以勇決知名。

translations.literal: Ben endorsed the plan, ultimately broke the bandits, and thereby became known for courage and decisiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Ben urged the plan on him, broke the bandits in the end, and from that day was known for bold resolve.

sentences.zh: 起家州主簿。

translations.literal: He began his career as chief clerk of the province.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as the province's chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 及隋文帝作相，授丞相府大都督，領鄉兵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was still regent, he was appointed Senior Commander in the Chancellor's office and commanded local militia.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was still regent, Ben was made a senior commander in the chancellor's office and put in charge of local militia.

sentences.zh: 賀若弼之鎮江都也，特敕奫從，因為間諜。

translations.literal: When He Ruo Bi was stationed at Jiangdu, the emperor specially ordered Ben to accompany him and serve as a spy.
translations.idiomatic: When He Ruo Bi took post at Jiangdu, the emperor specially ordered Ben to go with him as a spy.

sentences.zh: 平陳之役，頗有力焉。

translations.literal: In the conquest of Chen he contributed considerable effort.
translations.idiomatic: In the conquest of Chen he did the state real service.

sentences.zh: 進位開府儀同三司，封文安縣子。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Opening Grandee of the First Order, Third Rank, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Wen'an County.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to opening grandee of the first order, third rank, and enfeoffed as viscount of Wen'an county.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，奫率水軍破逆賊笮子游於京口、薛子建於和州。

translations.literal: More than a year later Ben led the naval forces and defeated the rebel Ze Ziyou at Jingkou and Xue Zijian at Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: A year and more later Ben led the fleet, crushed the rebel Ze Ziyou at Jingkou, and Xue Zijian at Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 征入，拜大將軍。

translations.literal: Summoned to court, he was made Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Called to the capital, he was made grand general.

sentences.zh: 文帝命升御坐宴之，謂曰：「卿可為朕兒，朕為卿父。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen ordered him to ascend to the imperial seat for a feast and said: "You may be my son; I will be your father.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen had him take the imperial seat at a feast and said, "You may call yourself my son; I will call myself your father.

sentences.zh: 今日聚集，示無外也。

translations.literal: Today's gathering shows we keep no outsiders between us."
translations.idiomatic: This gathering today is to show that we keep no outsider between us."

sentences.zh: 」後賜綠沈甲、獸文具裝，綺羅千匹。

translations.literal: Later he was granted green-dyed armor, fittings in the form of beasts, and a thousand bolts of brocade and gauze.
translations.idiomatic: Later he received armor dyed deep green, harness worked with beast heads, and a thousand bolts of brocade and gauze.

sentences.zh: 尋從楊素征江表，別破高智慧於會稽，吳世華於臨海。

translations.literal: Soon after he followed Yang Su in the Jiangnan campaign and separately defeated Gao Zhihui at Kuaiji and Wu Shihua at Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he followed Yang Su in the Jiangnan campaign and on his own broke Gao Zhihui at Kuaiji and Wu Shihua at Linhai.

sentences.zh: 進位上大將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Upper Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to upper grand general.

sentences.zh: 曆撫、濟二州刺史，俱有能名。

translations.literal: He served successively as governor of Fuzhou and Jizhou, both with reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Fuzhou and Jizhou in turn, and in both earned a name for ability.

sentences.zh: 開皇十八年，為行軍總管，從漢王諒征遼東。

translations.literal: In Kaihuang 18 he was made campaign commander and followed Prince of Han Yang Liang against Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Kaihuang he was made campaign commander and followed the prince of Han, Yang Liang, against Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 諒軍多物故，奫眾獨全，帝善之。

translations.literal: Yang Liang's army suffered many deaths; Ben's forces alone remained intact, and the emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Liang's army lost men everywhere, but Ben's troops came through whole, and the emperor commended him.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，卒于潭州總管，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era he died as Grand Protector of Tanzhou; posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Renshou era he died while serving as grand protector of Tanzhou; his posthumous name was Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子孝廉。

translations.literal: His son Xiaolian.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xiaolian.

sentences.zh: 麥鐵杖，始興人也。

translations.literal: Mai Tiezhang was a native of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Mai Tiezhang came from Shixing.

sentences.zh: 貧賤，少勇驍，有膂力，日行五百里，走及奔馬。

translations.literal: Poor and lowly in youth, he was brave and fierce, with great physical strength; he could travel five hundred li in a day and keep pace with a galloping horse.
translations.idiomatic: Born poor and obscure, he was fierce and bold, with uncommon strength: he could cover five hundred li in a day and keep up with a galloping horse.

sentences.zh: 性疏誕使酒，好交遊，重信義，每以漁獵為事，不修生業。

translations.literal: He was unrestrained and fond of drink, loved company and valued loyalty; he lived by fishing and hunting and did not maintain a settled livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: He was wild and given to wine, loved companions and kept his word, and lived by fishing and hunting without ever settling to honest trade.

sentences.zh: 陳大建中，結聚為群盜，廣州刺史歐陽頠俘之以獻，沒為官戶，配執禦傘。

translations.literal: In the Dajian era of Chen he banded together as a raider chief; Ouyang Hui, governor of Guangzhou, captured him and presented him to the court; he was made a government bondservant and assigned to hold the imperial parasol.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chen, in the Dajian era, he gathered a band of robbers. Ouyang Hui, governor of Guangzhou, took him and sent him up; he was made a bondservant of the state and set to carry the imperial parasol.

sentences.zh: 每罷朝後，行百餘里，夜至南徐州，窬城而入，行光火劫盜。

translations.literal: After each court dismissal he would go more than a hundred li, reach Southern Xuzhou by night, climb the wall, and commit torchlit robbery.
translations.idiomatic: After court each day he would run more than a hundred li, reach Southern Xuzhou by night, scale the wall, and rob houses by torchlight.

sentences.zh: 旦還，及牙時，仍又執傘。

translations.literal: By dawn he would return, and when the procession assembled he would again hold the parasol.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn he was back, and when the imperial procession formed he was again holding the parasol.

sentences.zh: 如此者十餘度，物主識之，州以狀奏。

translations.literal: This happened more than ten times; the owners recognized him, and the province reported it in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He did this more than ten times. The victims recognized him, and the province sent up a report.

sentences.zh: 朝士見鐵杖每旦恆在，弗之信。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen saw Tiezhang at dawn every day and would not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Men at court saw Tiezhang at his post every morning and refused to believe the charge.

sentences.zh: 後南徐州數告變，尚書蔡征曰：「此可驗矣。

translations.literal: Later Southern Xuzhou reported disturbances repeatedly; Minister Cai Zheng said: "This can be put to the test."
translations.idiomatic: Later Southern Xuzhou sent repeated alarms of trouble. Minister Cai Zheng said, "We can put this to proof."

sentences.zh: 」于仗下時，購以百金，求人送詔書與南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: At the time of the weapons guard formation he offered a hundred in gold to whoever would deliver an imperial edict to the governor of Southern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the formation below the imperial weapons guard he offered a hundred in gold to anyone who would carry an edict to the governor of Southern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 鐵杖出應募，齎敕而往，明旦反奏事。

translations.literal: Tiezhang came forward to accept the mission, carried the edict and went, and the next morning reported back at court.
translations.idiomatic: Tiezhang answered the call, took the edict and went, and the next morning was back at court to report.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「信然，為盜明矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "It is true—he is clearly the thief."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "So it is true—he is plainly the thief."

sentences.zh: 」惜其勇捷，誡而釋之。

translations.literal: Yet cherishing his courage and speed, he admonished him and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor prized his daring and speed, warned him, and let him go.

sentences.zh: 陳亡後，徙居清流縣。

translations.literal: After Chen fell he moved to Qingliu county.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Chen he moved to Qingliu county.

sentences.zh: 遇江東反，楊素遣鐵杖頭戴草束，夜浮度江，覘賊中消息，具知還報。

translations.literal: When rebellion broke out east of the Yangtze, Yang Su sent Tiezhang with a bundle of grass on his head to float across the river by night, spy out the rebels' dispositions, learn everything, and return to report.
translations.idiomatic: When the lower Yangtze rose in revolt, Yang Su sent Tiezhang with a sheaf of grass on his head to swim the river by night, learn the rebels' strength, and bring word back.

sentences.zh: 後復更往，為賊所禽，逆帥李稜縛送高智慧。

translations.literal: He went again and was captured by the rebels; the rebel chief Li Ling bound him and sent him to Gao Zhihui.
translations.idiomatic: He went again and was taken by the rebels; their leader Li Ling bound him and sent him to Gao Zhihui.

sentences.zh: 行至庱亭，衛者憩食，哀其餒，解手以給其餐。

translations.literal: When they reached Chengting the escorts paused to eat; pitying his hunger, one loosened his bonds to give him food.
translations.idiomatic: At Chengting the guards stopped to eat. One, pitying his hunger, loosened his bonds to give him a meal.

sentences.zh: 鐵杖取賊刀亂斬衛者，殺之皆盡，悉割其鼻，懷之以歸。

translations.literal: Tiezhang seized the guards' swords and hacked them down, killing every one; he cut off all their noses and brought them back in his coat.
translations.idiomatic: Tiezhang snatched their swords, cut the guards down to the last man, sliced off every nose, and carried them home in his robe.

sentences.zh: 素大奇之。

translations.literal: Yang Su was greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 後敘戰勳，不及鐵杖，遇素馳驛歸於京師，鐵杖步追之，每夜則同宿。

translations.literal: Later when battle merits were recorded Tiezhang was left out; he caught up with Yang Su's post-horse galloping back to the capital, keeping pace on foot and lodging with him each night.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when battle honors were entered, Tiezhang was passed over. He ran after Yang Su's post-horse all the way to the capital, keeping up on foot and sharing his lodging each night.

sentences.zh: 素見而悟，特奏授儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Yang Su saw him he understood and specially memorialized to grant him Opening Grandee of the Third Order.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Su saw him he understood, and by special memorial had him made opening grandee of the third order.

sentences.zh: 以不識書，放還鄉里。

translations.literal: Because he could not read, he was sent back to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Because he could not read, he was sent home.

sentences.zh: 成陽公李徹稱其驍武，開皇十六年，徵至京師，除車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Duke Li Che of Chengyang praised his martial prowess; in Kaihuang 16 he was summoned to the capital and made Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: Li Che, duke of Chengyang, praised his fighting power; in the sixteenth year of Kaihuang he was called to the capital and made cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 仍從楊素北征突厥，加上開府。

translations.literal: He again followed Yang Su on the northern campaign against the Turks and was made Upper Opening Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Yang Su north against the Turks and was made upper opening grandee.

sentences.zh: 鐵杖自以荷恩深重，每懷竭命之志。

translations.literal: Tiezhang felt himself deeply bound by grace and always harbored the will to give his life.
translations.idiomatic: Tiezhang felt the court's favor heavy upon him and always kept the will to spend his life in return.

sentences.zh: 及遼東之役，請為前鋒，顧謂醫者吳景賢曰：「大丈夫性命自有所在，豈能艾炷灸頞，瓜釭袴鼻，療黃不差，而臥死兒女手中乎！

translations.literal: At the Liaodong campaign he asked to serve as vanguard and told the physician Wu Jingxian: "A great man's life has its own place—how could I have moxa burned on my forehead and a melon rind tied to my nose for jaundice that will not heal, only to die abed in the hands of wife and children!"
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong campaign he asked for the vanguard and told the physician Wu Jingxian, "A true man's death has its proper place. Am I to have moxa burned on my brow and a melon rind bound on my nose for jaundice that will not clear, then die in bed in the hands of wife and children?"

sentences.zh: 」將度遼，呼其三子曰：「阿奴！

translations.literal: About to cross the Liao, he called his three sons: "My boys!"
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to cross the Liao, he called his three sons: "Boys!"

sentences.zh: 當備淺色黃衫。

translations.literal: Prepare light-colored yellow shirts.
translations.idiomatic: "Keep light yellow shirts ready."

sentences.zh: 吾荷國恩，今是死日。

translations.literal: I owe the state's grace; today is the day I die.
translations.idiomatic: "I owe the state a great debt; today is the day I die."

sentences.zh: 我得被殺，爾當富貴。

translations.literal: If I am killed, you will grow rich.
translations.idiomatic: "If I am slain, you will grow rich."

sentences.zh: 唯誠與孝，爾其勉之。

translations.literal: Only be sincere and filial—strive in that.
translations.idiomatic: "Only be loyal and filial—do your utmost in that."

sentences.zh: 」及濟，橋未成，去東岸尚數丈，賊大至。

translations.literal: When they crossed, the bridge was not yet finished and they were still several zhang from the east bank when the enemy came in great force.
translations.idiomatic: When they crossed, the bridge was not yet complete and they were still several zhang from the east bank when the enemy came in force.

sentences.zh: 杖跳上岸，與賊戰，死。

translations.literal: Tiezhang leaped ashore with his staff and fought the enemy until he died.
translations.idiomatic: Tiezhang sprang ashore with his iron staff, fought the enemy, and fell.

sentences.zh: 武賁郎將錢士雄、孟金叉亦死之，左右更無及者。

translations.literal: Guard officers Qian Shixiong and Meng Jincha also died; none on either flank could keep up with them.
translations.idiomatic: The guard officers Qian Shixiong and Meng Jincha died as well; no one on either side could match their pace.

sentences.zh: 帝為之流涕，購得其屍，贈光祿大夫、宿國公，諡曰武烈。

translations.literal: The emperor wept; a reward was set for his corpse; he was posthumously made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Duke of Su State, posthumous name Wulie.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept, set a price on his body, and posthumously made him grand master for splendid happiness and duke of Su, with the posthumous name Wulie.

sentences.zh: 子孟才嗣，授光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His son Mengcai succeeded and was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mengcai inherited the line and was made grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 孟才二弟仲才、季才，俱拜正議大夫。

translations.literal: Mengcai's two younger brothers Zhongcai and Jicai were both made Correcting Counselors.
translations.idiomatic: Mengcai's younger brothers Zhongcai and Jicai were both made rectifying grand masters.

sentences.zh: 賵贈钜萬，賜轀輬車，給前後部羽葆鼓吹。

translations.literal: Funerary gifts amounted to tens of thousands; a wheeled hearse was granted, with feathered banners and pipes before and behind.
translations.idiomatic: Funerary gifts ran to tens of thousands; he was given a wheeled hearse and feathered banners and pipes before and behind.

sentences.zh: 命平壤道敗將宇文述等百餘人皆為執紼，王公以下送至郊外。

translations.literal: More than a hundred defeated generals of the Pyongyang campaign route, including Yuwen Shu, were ordered to hold the mourning cords; nobles and officials escorted the funeral beyond the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred defeated generals of the Pyongyang route, Yuwen Shu among them, were ordered to pull the mourning cords; princes and officials escorted the bier beyond the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 士雄贈左光祿大夫、右屯衛將軍、武強侯，諡曰剛。

translations.literal: Shixiong was posthumously made Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Right Dwelling Guard General, Marquis of Wuqiang, posthumous name Gang.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong was posthumously made left grand master for splendid happiness, right dwelling guard general, and marquis of Wuqiang, with the posthumous name Gang.

sentences.zh: 子傑嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jie succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jie succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 金叉贈右光祿大夫，子善誼襲官。

translations.literal: Jincha was posthumously made Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; his son Shanyi inherited the office.
translations.idiomatic: Jincha was posthumously made right grand master for splendid happiness; his son Shanyi inherited his post.

sentences.zh: 孟才，字智稜，果烈有父風，帝以其死節將子，恩錫殊厚，拜武賁郎將。

translations.literal: Mengcai, styled Zhileng, was fierce and resolute in his father's manner. The emperor, because of his father's death in loyalty, showed his son extraordinary favor and made him a Guard Officer of the Feathered Retinue.
translations.idiomatic: Mengcai, courtesy name Zhileng, was fierce and resolute like his father. Because the father had died loyal, the emperor heaped favor on the son and made him an officer of the feathered guard.

sentences.zh: 及江都之難，慨然有復仇志。

translations.literal: At the catastrophe at Jiangdu he was stirred to thoughts of revenge.
translations.idiomatic: At the disaster at Jiangdu he burned to take revenge.

sentences.zh: 與武牙郎將錢傑素交友，二人相謂曰：「事等世荷國恩，門著誠節。

translations.literal: He was close friends with Guard Tooth Officer Qian Jie; the two said to each other: "Our house has received the state's grace for generations and is known for loyal service.
translations.idiomatic: He was sworn friends with the guard tooth officer Qian Jie. The two said to each other, "Our house has eaten the state's rice for generations and is known for loyal service.

sentences.zh: 今賊臣殺逆，社稷淪亡，無節可紀，何面目視息世間哉！

translations.literal: Now a traitorous minister has murdered the sovereign and the altars are ruined; we have no integrity left to record—what face have we to draw breath in the world!"
translations.idiomatic: Now a traitor has killed the ruler and the altars lie in ruin. We have no honor left to set down—what face have we to go on breathing in this world?"

sentences.zh: 」乃流涕扼腕，相與謀于顯福宮邀擊宇文化及。

translations.literal: They wept, wrung their wrists, and together plotted at Xianfu Palace to ambush Yuwen Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: They wept, clenched their wrists, and together plotted at Xianfu Palace to waylay Yuwen Huaji.

sentences.zh: 事臨發，陳籓之子謙知而告之，與其党沈光俱為化及所害，忠義之士哀焉。

translations.literal: When the affair was about to break, Chen Fan's son Qian learned of it and informed them; he and his comrade Shen Guang were both killed by Huaji—men of loyalty mourned them.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was about to move, Chen Fan's son Qian learned of it and told; he and his comrade Shen Guang were both killed by Huaji, and men of honor grieved for them.

sentences.zh: 光字總持，吳興人也。

translations.literal: Guang, styled Zongchi, was a native of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Guang, courtesy name Zongchi, came from Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 父居道，仕陳為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Judao served Chen as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His father Judao had served Chen as vice minister of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 陳滅，徙家長安。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, the family moved to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, the family moved to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 皇太子勇引署學士。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yong appointed him as a scholar in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yong took him on as a scholar in attendance.

sentences.zh: 後為漢王諒府掾，諒敗，除名。

translations.literal: Later he served as an aide in the household of the Prince of Han, Liang; when Liang was defeated, he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as an aide in Prince Liang of Han's household; when Liang was defeated, he was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 光少驍捷，善戲馬，為天下之最。

translations.literal: In youth Guang was swift and agile, skilled at horsemanship and acrobatics on horseback, the finest under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Guang was swift and fierce, a master of trick riding unmatched under heaven.

sentences.zh: 略綜書記，微有詞藻，常慕立功名，不拘小節。

translations.literal: He had some command of letters and records, a modest gift for phrasing, and always yearned to win merit and make a name, heedless of small proprieties.
translations.idiomatic: He had some schooling in letters and a modest gift for phrasing, and always burned to win glory and leave a name, careless of small proprieties.

sentences.zh: 家貧，父兄並以傭書為事，光獨跅昞朷，交通輕俠，為京師惡少年所附。

translations.literal: His family was poor; father and elder brothers all hired themselves out as copyists, while Guang alone was unrestrained, consorting with daredevils and light cavaliers, and was taken up by the capital's worst young ruffians.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor; father and brothers lived by copying books for hire, while Guang alone ran wild, keeping company with swashbucklers and was followed by the capital's worst young blades.

sentences.zh: 人多贍遺，得以養親，每致甘食美服，未嘗困匱。

translations.literal: Many gave him gifts, so he could support his parents; he always provided fine food and handsome clothes and never knew want.
translations.idiomatic: Many lavished gifts on him, enough to support his parents; he always brought them fine food and good clothes and never knew want.

sentences.zh: 初建禪定寺，其中幡竿高十餘丈，適值繩絕，非人力所及。

translations.literal: When Chanding Temple was first built, its banner pole stood more than ten zhang high; the rope had just broken and no human strength could reach it.
translations.idiomatic: When Chanding Temple was first built, its banner pole rose more than ten zhang; the rope had just snapped and no one on the ground could reach it.

sentences.zh: 光謂僧曰：「當相為上繩。

translations.literal: Guang told the monks, "I will get a rope up for you."
translations.idiomatic: Guang told the monks, "I will get a rope up there for you."

sentences.zh: 」與諸僧驚喜。

translations.literal: The monks were startled and delighted.
translations.idiomatic: The monks were astonished and overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 光因取索口銜，拍竿而上，直至龍頭。

translations.literal: Guang took a rope in his teeth, struck the pole and climbed up, all the way to the dragon head.
translations.idiomatic: Guang took a rope in his teeth, struck the pole and climbed, straight to the dragon head at the top.

sentences.zh: 擊繩畢，手足皆放，透空而下，以掌拓地，倒行十餘步。

translations.literal: When the rope was fixed, he let go with hands and feet, dropped through the air, broke his fall with his palms on the ground, and walked backward more than ten paces.
translations.idiomatic: When the rope was set, he let go with hands and feet, fell through open air, broke the impact with his palms on the ground, and walked backward more than ten paces.

sentences.zh: 觀者駭悅，莫不嗟異，時人號為「肉飛仙」。

translations.literal: Spectators were awed and delighted; all marveled, and men of the time called him "the flesh-flying immortal."
translations.idiomatic: The crowd was thrilled and amazed; everyone exclaimed in wonder, and men of the time called him the Flesh-Flying Immortal.

sentences.zh: 大業中，煬帝征天下驍果之士伐遼東，光預焉。

translations.literal: In the Daye era, Emperor Yang summoned the empire's fiercest warriors for the Liaodong campaign; Guang was among them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye reign, Emperor Yang called up the empire's fiercest fighters for the Liaodong war, and Guang was among them.

sentences.zh: 同類數萬人，皆出其下。

translations.literal: Among tens of thousands of his kind, all ranked below him.
translations.idiomatic: Among tens of thousands of the same breed, all stood beneath him.

sentences.zh: 光將詣行在所，賓客送至灞上百餘騎。

translations.literal: As Guang set out for the imperial camp, guests escorted him with more than a hundred riders to Ba River.
translations.idiomatic: When Guang set out for the emperor's camp, friends and clients rode more than a hundred strong to see him off at Ba River.

sentences.zh: 光酹酒誓曰：「是行若不建功立名，當死於高麗，不復與諸君相見。

translations.literal: Guang poured a libation and swore: "On this march, if I do not win merit and make a name, let me die in Goguryeo and never see you again."
translations.idiomatic: Guang poured wine and swore, "On this campaign, if I do not win merit and make a name, let me die in Goguryeo and never face you again."

sentences.zh: 」及從帝攻遼東，以沖梯擊城，竿長十五丈，光升其端，臨城與賊戰，知兵接敵，殺傷十數人。

translations.literal: When he followed the emperor to storm Liaodong, using a siege tower whose pole was fifteen zhang long, he climbed to its top, fought at the wall with the enemy, met troops in battle, and killed or wounded more than ten.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed the emperor against Liaodong, he rode a battering tower fifteen zhang tall to its summit, fought atop the wall with the enemy, met them blade to blade, and killed or wounded more than ten.

sentences.zh: 賊競擊而墜，未及地，適遇竿有垂絙，光接而復上。

translations.literal: The enemy pressed him and he fell; before he reached the ground he grasped a hanging cord on the pole and climbed up again.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy swarmed him and he fell; before he hit the ground he caught a dangling cord on the pole and hauled himself up again.

sentences.zh: 帝望見，壯而異之，馳召與語，大悅，即日拜朝散大夫，賜寶刀良馬。

translations.literal: The emperor saw it, admired and marveled, summoned him at a gallop to speak, was greatly pleased, and that same day made him Palace Attendant Grandee, granting a treasured blade and fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw it, was stirred and astonished, galloped to call him and speak with him, was deeply pleased, and that same day made him palace attendant grandee, with a treasured saber and fine horses.

sentences.zh: 恆置左右，親顧漸密。

translations.literal: He was kept ever at the emperor's side; royal favor grew intimate.
translations.idiomatic: He was kept constantly at the emperor's side, and imperial favor drew ever closer.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以為折沖郎將，賞遇優重。

translations.literal: Before long he was made General Who Breaks the Charge, with rewards and favor beyond the common.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made general who breaks the charge, with rewards and favor beyond any peer.

sentences.zh: 帝每推食解衣賜之，同輩莫比。

translations.literal: The emperor would share his food and give him his own garments; none among his peers could compare.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would push food toward him and strip off his own coat to give him; none among his fellows could compare.

sentences.zh: 光自以荷恩深重，思懷竭節。

translations.literal: Guang felt the grace laid upon him was profound and resolved to repay it with utter loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Guang felt the debt of grace was heavy and set his heart on repaying it to the last breath.

sentences.zh: 及江都之難，潛構義勇，將為帝復仇。

translations.literal: When the catastrophe at Jiangdu came, he secretly gathered men of righteous valor to avenge the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster struck at Jiangdu, he secretly rallied brave men to avenge the emperor.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝寵昵官奴，名為給使，宇文化及以光驍男，方任之，使總統，營于禁內。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had favored palace slaves called "appointed servants"; Yuwen Huaji, seeing Guang's fierce valor, had lately entrusted him to command them, camped within the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had favored palace slaves called appointed servants; Yuwen Huaji, seeing Guang's fierce mettle, had lately put him in command of them, encamped inside the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 時麥孟才、錢傑等陰圖化及，因謂光曰：「我等荷國厚恩，不能死難，又俯首事讎，受其驅率，何用生為！

translations.literal: At that time Mai Mengcai, Qian Jie, and others secretly plotted against Huaji, and said to Guang: "We have borne the state's deep grace and could not die in its calamity, yet now bow our heads to serve our foe's killer and obey his whip—what use is life?
translations.idiomatic: At that time Mai Mengcai, Qian Jie, and others were secretly plotting against Huaji, and said to Guang, "We have eaten the state's heavy grace and could not die in its ruin, yet now we bow to the murderer and take his orders. What is life worth?

sentences.zh: 吾必欲殺之，死無所恨。

translations.literal: We are determined to kill him; death will hold no regret."
translations.idiomatic: We mean to kill him, and death will hold no regret."

sentences.zh: 公義士也，肯從我乎？

translations.literal: You are a man of honor; will you follow us?"
translations.idiomatic: You are a man of honor. Will you join us?"

sentences.zh: 」光泣下沾衿曰：「是所望于將軍也。

translations.literal: Tears soaking his collar, Guang said: "That is what I have hoped to hear from you, General."
translations.idiomatic: Tears wet his robe as Guang said, "That is exactly what I have hoped to hear from you, General."

sentences.zh: 僕領給使數百人，並荷先帝恩，今在化及內營。

translations.literal: I lead several hundred appointed servants, all who owed grace to the late emperor, and they are now in Huaji's inner camp.
translations.idiomatic: I command several hundred appointed servants who all owed grace to the late emperor, and they are now in Huaji's inner camp.

sentences.zh: 以此復仇，如鷹鸇之逐烏雀。

translations.literal: With them to take revenge would be like eagles and falcons hunting sparrows."
translations.idiomatic: With them to take revenge would be like hawks and falcons falling on sparrows."

sentences.zh: 」孟才為將軍。

translations.literal: Mengcai was made general.
translations.idiomatic: Mengcai was made general.

sentences.zh: 領江淮眾數千人，期以營將發時，晨起襲化及。

translations.literal: He led several thousand men from Jiang-Huai, set to strike Huaji at dawn when the camp was about to march.
translations.idiomatic: He led several thousand men from the Jiang-Huai region, planning to strike Huaji at dawn when the camp was ready to break camp.

sentences.zh: 光語泄，陳謙告其事。

translations.literal: Guang's words leaked; Chen Qian reported the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Guang's words leaked out; Chen Qian reported the plot.

sentences.zh: 化及大懼曰：「此麥鐵杖子也，及沈光者，並勇決不可當，須避其鋒。

translations.literal: Huaji was greatly afraid and said: "This is Mai Tiezhang's son, and Shen Guang—these are fiercely resolute men none can withstand; we must avoid their edge."
translations.idiomatic: Huaji was deeply afraid and said, "This is Mai Tiezhang's son, and Shen Guang. Both are fierce and resolute beyond facing. We must avoid their edge."

sentences.zh: 」是夜即與腹心走出營外，留人告司馬德戡等，遣領兵馬，逮捕孟才。

translations.literal: That night he fled the camp with his intimates, left word for Sima Dekan and the rest to send troops and seize Mengcai.
translations.idiomatic: That night he slipped out of camp with his closest men, left word for Sima Dekan and the rest to bring troops and seize Mengcai.

sentences.zh: 光聞營內喧聲，知事發，不及被甲。

translations.literal: Guang heard uproar in the camp, knew the plot had broken, and had no time to don armor.
translations.idiomatic: Guang heard uproar inside the camp, knew the plot had failed, and had no time to arm himself.

sentences.zh: 即襲化及營，空無所獲。

translations.literal: He struck at Huaji's camp but found it empty.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed Huaji's camp and found it empty.

sentences.zh: 逢舍人元敏，數而斬之。

translations.literal: He met Attendant Yuan Min, reproached him, and cut him down.
translations.idiomatic: He met attendant Yuan Min, rebuked him, and cut him down.

sentences.zh: 德戡兵至，四面圍合。

translations.literal: Dekan's troops arrived and closed in on every side.
translations.idiomatic: Dekan's troops arrived and hemmed him in on every side.

sentences.zh: 光大呼潰圍，給使齊奮，斬首數十級，賊皆披靡。

translations.literal: Guang roared and broke the encirclement; the appointed servants fought as one, took dozens of heads, and the enemy scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Guang shouted and burst the ring; the appointed servants fought as one, took dozens of heads, and the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 德戡輒復遣騎，翼而射之。

translations.literal: Dekan again sent horsemen to flank him and shoot.
translations.idiomatic: Dekan sent horsemen again to ride on his flanks and shoot him down.

sentences.zh: 光身無介胄，遇害，時年二十八。

translations.literal: Guang wore no armor and was killed; he was twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Guang wore no armor and was killed. He was twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 麾下百人皆鬥死，一無降者。

translations.literal: A hundred men under his command all fought to the death; not one yielded.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred men under his command all fought to the death; not one surrendered.

sentences.zh: 壯士聞之，莫不為之隕涕。

translations.literal: When brave men heard of it, none failed to shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Brave men who heard of it could not keep back their tears.

sentences.zh: 權武，字武弄，天水人也。

translations.literal: Quan Wu, styled Wunong, was a native of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Wu, courtesy name Wunong, came from Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 祖超，魏秦州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chao was Wei governor of Qin province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chao had been Wei governor of Qin province.

sentences.zh: 父襲慶，仕周，為開府。

translations.literal: His father Xiqing served Zhou as a grand opening.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiqing had served Zhou as a grand opening.

sentences.zh: 時武元皇帝之為周將也，與齊師戰於并州。

translations.literal: In the days when Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou was a Zhou general, he fought Qi armies at Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the days when the Zhou emperor Wu Yuan was still a Zhou general, he fought Qi forces at Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 襲慶時從，被圍百餘重，力戰矢盡，短兵接戰，殺傷甚眾，刀槊皆折，脫胄擲地，向賊大罵曰：「何不來斫頭！

translations.literal: Xiqing was with him then, surrounded more than a hundred layers deep; he fought until his arrows were spent, closed in with short weapons, killed and wounded a great host; swords and spears all broke; he cast off his helmet, threw it to the ground, and shouted at the enemy: "Why do you not come and take my head!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiqing was with him then, trapped in more than a hundred rings of siege; he fought until his arrows were gone, closed to hand strokes, killed and wounded a great crowd; blades and spears snapped; he tore off his helmet, hurled it to the ground, and roared at the enemy, "Why do you not come and take my head!"

sentences.zh: 」賊遂殺之。

translations.literal: The enemy then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy then killed him.

sentences.zh: 武以忠臣子，起家拜開府，襲爵齊郡公。

translations.literal: As son of a loyal minister, Wu entered service as grand opening and inherited the title Marquis of Qi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: As the son of a loyal minister, Wu entered office as grand opening and inherited the marquisate of Qi commandery.

sentences.zh: 武少果勁，勇力絕人，能重甲上馬。

translations.literal: Wu in youth was resolute and fierce, his strength beyond other men; he could mount in full heavy armor.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Wu was hard and fierce, with strength beyond other men; he could vault into the saddle wearing full heavy armor.

sentences.zh: 嘗倒投于井，未及泉，復躍而出，其拳捷如此。

translations.literal: Once he plunged headfirst into a well; before he reached the water he leaped out again—such was his nimble power.
translations.idiomatic: Once he dove headfirst into a well; before he reached the water he sprang out again. Such was his quick strength.

sentences.zh: 頻以軍功增邑。

translations.literal: Repeatedly his fief was enlarged for military merit.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again his fief was enlarged for battlefield merit.

sentences.zh: 周宣帝時，拜勁捷左旅上大夫，進位上開府。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xuan of Zhou he was made Grand Master of the Left Swift Brigade and advanced to upper grand opening.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan of Zhou he was made grand master of the left swift brigade and advanced to upper grand opening.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝為丞相，引置左右。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister, he kept Wu at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister, he kept Wu close at hand.

sentences.zh: 平陳之役，以行軍總管從晉王出六合，還拜豫州刺史。

translations.literal: In the campaign to pacify Chen he served as mobile commander under the Prince of Jin, advancing to Liuhe; on return he was made governor of Yu province.
translations.idiomatic: In the pacification of Chen he served as mobile commander under the Prince of Jin, marching out through Liuhe; on his return he was made governor of Yu province.

sentences.zh: 以創業之舊，進位大將軍，檢校潭州總管。

translations.literal: For his service in founding the dynasty, he was raised to great general and acting area commander of Tan province.
translations.idiomatic: For his part in founding the dynasty, he was raised to great general and acting area commander of Tan province.

sentences.zh: 其年，桂州人李世賢作亂，武以行軍總管與武候大將軍虞慶則擊平之。

translations.literal: That year Li Shixian of Gui province rebelled; Wu as mobile commander, together with the martial sentinel great general Yu Qingze, crushed the revolt.
translations.idiomatic: That year Li Shixian of Gui province rose in revolt; Wu as mobile commander, with the martial sentinel great general Yu Qingze, put the rebellion down.

sentences.zh: 慶則以罪誅，功竟不錄，復還於州。

translations.literal: Qingze was executed for a crime; Wu's achievements went unrecorded, and he returned to his province.
translations.idiomatic: Qingze was executed for a crime; Wu's merit went uncredited, and he returned to his province.

sentences.zh: 多造金帶，遣嶺南酋領，其人復答以寶物，武皆納之，由是致富。

translations.literal: He had many gold belts made and sent them to chieftains of the southern mountains; they replied with treasures, and Wu took them all in, growing rich thereby.
translations.idiomatic: He had many gold belts forged and sent them to chieftains beyond the southern ranges; they sent back treasures in return, and Wu accepted them all, growing wealthy thereby.

sentences.zh: 後武晚生一子，與親客宴集，酒酣，遂擅赦所部獄囚。

translations.literal: Later Wu had a son in his old age; feasting with close guests, deep in wine he unauthorizedly released prisoners in his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wu fathered a son in his old age; at a feast with close guests, drunk, he on his own authority freed prisoners in his command.

sentences.zh: 武常以南越邊遠，政從其俗，務適便宜，不依律令，而每言當今法急，官不可為。

translations.literal: Wu often said that the southern Yue frontier was remote, that government should follow local custom and seek what was expedient, not cling to statutes—and that the laws of the day were harsh and office unbearable.
translations.idiomatic: Wu often said that the far southern Yue border should be ruled by local custom, with what worked rather than the code, and that the laws of the day were too tight for any man to hold office.

sentences.zh: 上令有案之，皆驗，令斬之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered an investigation; all was verified, and he commanded execution.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered an inquiry; every charge was proved, and he commanded Wu's execution.

sentences.zh: 武於獄中上書，言父為武元皇帝戰死于馬前，以求哀，由是除名。

translations.literal: From prison Wu submitted a memorial saying his father had died fighting before Emperor Wu's horse, begging mercy; thereby he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: From prison Wu sent up a memorial saying his father had died fighting before Emperor Wu Yuan's horse, begging pity; for that he was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，復拜大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era he was again made great general.
translations.idiomatic: In the Renshou era he was again made great general.

sentences.zh: 封邑如舊。

translations.literal: His fief was restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was restored as before.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授太子右衛率。

translations.literal: Before long he was made right leader of the crown prince's guard.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made right leader of the crown prince's guard.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，拜右武衛將軍，坐事免。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Wu was made general of the right martial guard but was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Wu was made general of the right martial guard, then dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 後為右屯衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was made great general of the right garrison guard.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made great general of the right garrison guard.

sentences.zh: 坐事除名。

translations.literal: For an offense he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense he was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 子弘。

translations.literal: His son was Hong.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Hong.

sentences.zh: 王仁恭，字元實，天水上邽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Rengong, styled Yuanshi, was a native of Shanggui in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rengong, courtesy name Yuanshi, came from Shanggui in Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 祖建，周鳳州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jian was Zhou governor of Feng province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jian had been Zhou governor of Feng province.

sentences.zh: 父猛，鄯州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Meng was governor of Shan province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Meng had been governor of Shan province.

sentences.zh: 仁恭少剛毅修謹，工騎射。

translations.literal: Rengong in youth was stern, resolute, and careful in conduct, skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Rengong was firm, disciplined, and skilled in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 秦孝王引為記室，後為車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Prince Xiao of Qin took him as recorder; later he was made general of chariots and cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao of Qin took him on as recorder; later he was made general of chariots and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 從楊素擊突厥于靈武，以功拜上開府。

translations.literal: He followed Yang Su against the Turks at Lingwu and for merit was made upper grand opening.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Yang Su against the Turks at Lingwu and, for merit, was made upper grand opening.

sentences.zh: 以驃騎將軍典蜀王軍事。

translations.literal: As general of swift cavalry he managed the military affairs of the Prince of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: As general of swift cavalry he oversaw the Prince of Shu's military affairs.

sentences.zh: 蜀王以罪廢，官屬多罹其患。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shu was deposed for a crime; many of his staff suffered in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shu was deposed for a crime, and many of his staff were caught in the fallout.

sentences.zh: 上以仁恭素質直，置而不問。

translations.literal: The emperor, knowing Rengong's plain upright character, set the matter aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, knowing Rengong's plain and upright nature, let the matter drop without inquiry.

sentences.zh: 後從楊素討平漢王諒，以功進位大將軍。

translations.literal: Later he followed Yang Su in crushing Prince of Han Liang and for merit was raised to great general.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Yang Su in putting down Prince Liang of Han and, for merit, was raised to great general.

sentences.zh: 曆呂、衛二州刺史。

translations.literal: He served as governor of Lü and Wei provinces in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as governor of Lü and Wei provinces.

sentences.zh: 尋改為汲郡太守，有能名。

translations.literal: Soon he was made prefect of Ji commandery and won a name for capability.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made prefect of Ji commandery and earned a name for able rule.

sentences.zh: 上征入朝，慰勉之，褒賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Summoned to court, he was comforted and encouraged, with rich rewards and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Called to court, he was comforted and praised, with rich rewards and gifts.

sentences.zh: 遷信都太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be prefect of Xin commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Xin commandery.

sentences.zh: 汲郡吏民扣馬號哭於道，數日不得出境。

translations.literal: Officials and people of Ji commandery seized his horse and wept along the road for days, so he could not leave the border.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners of Ji commandery seized his horse and wept in the road for days, so he could not cross the border.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，以仁恭為軍將。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign Rengong was made army commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong war Rengong was made an army commander.

sentences.zh: 及班師，仁恭為殿，遇賊，敗之。

translations.literal: On the return march Rengong commanded the rear guard; he met bandits and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On the withdrawal Rengong held the rear; he met raiders and beat them.

sentences.zh: 進左光祿大夫，明年，復以軍將指扶餘道，帝謂曰：「往者諸軍多不利，公獨以一軍破賊。

translations.literal: He was advanced to left grand master of the palace; the next year he was again made army commander on the Fuyu route. The emperor said: "In the past many armies fared badly, yet you alone with one army broke the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to left grand master of the palace; the next year he was again made army commander on the Fuyu route. The emperor said, "Before, many armies came to grief, yet you alone with one army broke the enemy."

sentences.zh: 古人云，敗軍之將不可以言勇，諸將其可任乎？

translations.literal: The ancients said a general of a defeated army may not speak of courage—can the other commanders be trusted?"
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said a beaten general should not talk of courage. Can the other commanders be trusted?"

sentences.zh: 今委公為前軍。

translations.literal: Now I entrust you as vanguard."
translations.idiomatic: Now I entrust the vanguard to you."

sentences.zh: 」前後賞賚甚重。

translations.literal: Rewards before and after were very heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards before and after were lavish.

sentences.zh: 仁恭遂進軍。

translations.literal: Rengong then advanced the army.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong then marched the army forward.

sentences.zh: 至新城，破其軍，因圍之。

translations.literal: Reaching Xincheng, he broke their army and besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: At Xincheng he shattered their army and laid siege to the city.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之大悅，遣賜以珍物，進光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and was greatly pleased; he sent rare gifts and advanced him to grand master of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and was greatly pleased; he sent rare gifts and raised him to grand master of the palace.

sentences.zh: 會楊玄感反，其兄子武賁郎將仲伯預焉，由是坐免。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, his nephew the guard officer Zhongbo took part; for this Rengong was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, his nephew the guard officer Zhongbo was implicated; for that Rengong was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 尋而突厥為寇，詔仁恭以本官領馬邑太守。

translations.literal: Soon after, when the Turks raided, an edict made Rengong, in his former office, also prefect of Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Turks raided; an edict appointed Rengong, in his former rank, to serve also as prefect of Mayi.

sentences.zh: 其年，始畢可汗來寇馬邑，復令二將勒兵南過。

translations.literal: That year the Shibi Qaghan came to raid Mayi; he again ordered two generals to lead troops south across the border.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Shibi qaghan came against Mayi; he again ordered two generals to drive their troops south across the frontier.

sentences.zh: 時郡兵不滿三千，仁恭簡精銳逆擊，破之，並斬二將。

translations.literal: At the time the commandery troops numbered fewer than three thousand; Rengong picked elite men for a counterattack, routed them, and beheaded both generals together.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery had fewer than three thousand troops; Rengong handpicked crack men for a counterstroke, smashed them, and took both generals' heads.

sentences.zh: 後突厥復入定襄，仁恭復大破之。

translations.literal: Later the Turks again invaded Dingxiang; Rengong again inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks later invaded Dingxiang again, and Rengong routed them once more.

sentences.zh: 時天下大亂，道路隔絕，仁恭頗改舊節，受納貨賄，又不敢輒開倉賑恤百姓。

translations.literal: The realm was in great turmoil and roads were cut off; Rengong greatly changed his former rectitude, accepted bribes, and yet dared not rashly open granaries to relieve the people.
translations.idiomatic: With the empire in chaos and the roads severed, Rengong slackened his old standards, took bribes, and still dared not open the granaries to feed the people.

sentences.zh: 其麾下校尉劉武周與仁恭侍婢奸通，恐其事泄，遂害之。

translations.literal: His staff commander Liu Wuzhou had illicit relations with Rengong's maidservant; fearing the affair would leak, he killed him.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinate commander Liu Wuzhou was sleeping with Rengong's maidservant; fearing exposure, he murdered him.

sentences.zh: 武周於是開倉賑給，郡內皆從之，自稱天子，置百官，轉攻傍郡。

translations.literal: Wuzhou then opened the granaries to give relief; the whole commandery followed him. He styled himself Son of Heaven, set up the hundred offices, and turned to attack neighboring commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou opened the granaries and gave out grain; the whole commandery rallied to him. He declared himself emperor, appointed officials, and marched on neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 吐萬緒，字長緒，代郡鮮卑人也。

translations.literal: Tuwu Xu, styled Changxu, was a Xianbei of Dai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Tuwu Xu, courtesy name Changxu, was a Xianbei from Dai commandery.

sentences.zh: 父通，周郢州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Tong had been governor of Ying in Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tong had served as governor of Ying under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 緒少有武略，在周，襲爵元壽縣公，累遷大將軍、小司武。

translations.literal: Xu in youth had martial aptitude; under Zhou he inherited the title Duke of Yuanshou and rose in succession to great general and Junior Director of Martial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Xu showed martial talent; under the Zhou he inherited the title Duke of Yuanshou and rose to great general and junior director of martial affairs.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，拜襄州總管，封穀城郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he was made Governor-General of Xiangzhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Gucheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Xu was made governor-general of Xiangzhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Gucheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 轉青州總管，頗有政名。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor-General of Qingzhou and won a name for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Qingzhou as governor-general, he earned a reputation for capable rule.

sentences.zh: 徙朔州總管，甚為北狄所憚。

translations.literal: He was moved to Governor-General of Shuozhou; the northern barbarians greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to Shuozhou as governor-general, he was deeply feared by the northern tribes.

sentences.zh: 後帝有吞陳志，轉為徐州總管，令修戰具。

translations.literal: Later, as the emperor harbored the plan to swallow Chen, he was made Governor-General of Xuzhou and ordered to ready war gear.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor set his sights on conquering Chen, Xu was posted to Xuzhou as governor-general and ordered to prepare for war.

sentences.zh: 及大舉濟江，緒以行軍總管與四河紇豆陵洪景屯兵江北。

translations.literal: When the great army crossed the Yangtze, Xu as campaign commander with Hedouling Hongjing of the Si River line held troops on the north bank of the river.
translations.idiomatic: During the great crossing of the Yangtze, Xu served as campaign commander alongside Hedouling Hongjing of the Si River line, holding the north bank.

sentences.zh: 及陳平，拜夏州總管。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, he was made Governor-General of Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen fell, he was made governor-general of Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣為太子，引為右虞候率。

translations.literal: When Prince Jin Guang became crown prince, he was brought in as Right Commander of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Guang of Jin became heir apparent, Xu was appointed right commander of the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 及帝即位，恐漢王諒為變，拜緒晉、絳二州刺史。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, fearing Prince of Han Liang might rebel, he appointed Xu governor of Jin and Jiang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession the emperor, fearing revolt from Prince Liang of Han, made Xu governor of Jin and Jiang provinces.

sentences.zh: 未出關，諒已舉兵，詔緒從楊素擊破之，拜左武候將軍。

translations.literal: Before he had left the passes, Liang had already raised troops; an edict ordered Xu to follow Yang Su and crush him, and he was made General of the Left Martial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Before Xu had cleared the passes, Liang was already in arms; an edict sent him after Yang Su to crush the revolt, and he was made general of the left martial guards.

sentences.zh: 大業初，轉光祿卿。

translations.literal: At the start of Daye he was transferred to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Daye reign he was made grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 賀若弼遇讒，引緒為證，緒明其無罪，由是免官。

translations.literal: He Ruo Bi fell under slander; he cited Xu as witness; Xu testified to his innocence, and for this was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: When He Ruo Bi was slandered, he called on Xu to testify; Xu cleared him, and for that Xu himself was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 後守東平太守。

translations.literal: Later he served as Administrator of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as administrator of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 帝幸江都，路經其境，迎謁道傍。

translations.literal: When the emperor went to Jiangdu and passed through his district, Xu welcomed and attended him by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled to Jiangdu through his territory, Xu met him by the road and paid his respects.

sentences.zh: 帝命升龍舟，緒因頓首謝往事。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him aboard the dragon boat; Xu bowed his head in thanks for past events.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had him board the imperial dragon boat; Xu kowtowed in gratitude for past kindness.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，拜金紫光祿大夫，太守如故。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and made him Grand Master with Golden Girdle, retaining the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and made him grand master with golden girdle while keeping him at his post.

sentences.zh: 及遼東之役，請為先鋒，拜左屯衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he asked to be vanguard and was made Great General of the Left Guards of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong war he volunteered for the vanguard and was made great general of the left household guards.

sentences.zh: 指蓋馬道。

translations.literal: He pointed to the Gaima route.
translations.idiomatic: He pointed the army toward the Gaima route.

sentences.zh: 及還，留鎮懷遠，進位左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On the return he was left to guard Huaiyuan and advanced to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: On the withdrawal he was left to hold Huaiyuan and promoted to left grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 時劉元進作亂，攻潤州，帝徵緒討之。

translations.literal: Liu Yuanjin rebelled and attacked Runzhou; the emperor summoned Xu to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yuanjin rose and besieged Runzhou, the emperor summoned Xu to put him down.

sentences.zh: 緒擊破元進，解潤州圍。

translations.literal: Xu broke Yuanjin and lifted the siege of Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu shattered Yuanjin and broke the siege of Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊窮蹙請降，元進及其偽僕射硃燮僅以身免，於陣斬其偽僕射管崇及其將軍陸顗等五千餘人。

translations.literal: The rebels, cornered, begged surrender; Yuanjin and his false vice-minister Zhu Xie barely escaped with their lives; on the battlefield he slew the false vice-minister Guan Chong and the general Lu Yan and more than five thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, the rebels sued for peace; Yuanjin and his false vice-minister Zhu Xie barely escaped; on the field Xu cut down the false vice-minister Guan Chong, the general Lu Yan, and more than five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 進解會稽圍。

translations.literal: He relieved the siege of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He lifted the siege of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 元進復據建安，帝令進討之。

translations.literal: Yuanjin again held Jian'an; the emperor ordered Xu to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjin seized Jian'an again; the emperor ordered Xu to pursue him.

sentences.zh: 緒以士卒疲弊，請息甲待來春。

translations.literal: Xu, seeing the troops weary, asked to rest the army and wait until spring.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the troops exhausted, Xu asked to stand down until spring.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，密求緒罪，有司奏緒怯懦違詔，除名配防建安。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased; secretly he sought Xu's faults; the ministry memorialized that Xu was cowardly and had defied the edict; he was struck from the rolls and assigned to guard duty at Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and quietly hunted for fault in Xu; the ministry reported cowardice and disobedience; Xu was struck from the rolls and sent to garrison Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 尋徵詣行在所，緒鬱鬱不得志，還至永嘉，發疾而卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned to the itinerant court; Xu, sunk in gloom and without fulfillment, on reaching Yongjia fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled to the traveling court; brooding and unfulfilled, Xu fell ill at Yongjia and died.

sentences.zh: 董純，字德厚，隴西成紀人。

translations.literal: Dong Chun, styled Dehou, was a native of Chengji in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chun, courtesy name Dehou, came from Chengji in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 祖和，魏太子左衛率。

translations.literal: His grandfather He had been Left Commandant of the Heirs Apparent Guard in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather He had been left commandant of the heir apparent's guard under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父升，周柱國。

translations.literal: His father Sheng had been a pillar of state in Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sheng had been a pillar of state under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 純少有膂力，便弓馬。

translations.literal: Chun in youth had great strength and was skilled at bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Chun was immensely strong and a master of bow and horse.

sentences.zh: 仕周，位司禦上士、典馭下大夫。

translations.literal: He served Zhou, holding the posts of Superior Attendant of the Imperial Stables and Junior Master of the Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Zhou as superior attendant of the imperial stables and junior master of the stud.

sentences.zh: 從武帝平齊，拜儀同，進為大興縣侯。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Wu in pacifying Qi and was made Commissary-Equivalent; he advanced to Marquis of Daxing county.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Wu in the conquest of Qi, was made a commissary-equivalent, and rose to marquis of Daxing county.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，進爵漢曲縣公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, his enfeoffment was raised to Duke of Hanqu county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Chun was raised to duke of Hanqu county.

sentences.zh: 後以軍功，進位上開府。

translations.literal: Later, for military merit, he advanced to Upper Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for military merit, he was made upper pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 開皇末，以勞舊拜左衛將軍，改封順政縣公。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaihuang, for long service he was made General of the Left Guards and his fief was changed to Duke of Shunzheng county.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Kaihuang, rewarded for long service, he was made general of the left guards and his fief was changed to duke of Shunzheng county.

sentences.zh: 後從楊素平漢王諒，以功拜柱國，進爵郡公，再遷左驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: Later, following Yang Su in pacifying Prince of Han Liang, for merit he was made Pillar of State, advanced to Duke of a commandery, and again promoted to General of the Left Brave Cavaliers.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Yang Su against Prince Liang of Han; for merit he was made pillar of state, raised to commandery duke, and promoted again to general of the left brave cavaliers.

sentences.zh: 齊王暕之得罪，純坐與交通，帝譴之。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qi Min fell from favor, Chun was implicated for association with him; the emperor reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Min of Qi fell from grace, Chun was blamed for consorting with him; the emperor rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 純曰：「此數詣齊王者，以先帝、先後往在仁壽宮，置元德太子及齊王於膝上，謂臣曰：'汝好看此二兒，勿忘吾言。

translations.literal: Chun said, "These many visits to Prince of Qi were because when the Late Emperor and Late Empress were at Renshou Palace, they placed the Heir of Virtue and Prince of Qi on their knees and told me, 'You must look well to these two boys; do not forget my words.'
translations.idiomatic: Chun said, "I went often to Prince Qi because at Renshou Palace the late emperor and empress set the Heir of Virtue and Prince Qi on their knees and told me, 'Watch these two boys well; do not forget what I say.'

sentences.zh: ' 臣誠不敢忘先帝言。

translations.literal: I truly dare not forget the Late Emperor's words.
translations.idiomatic: I truly have not forgotten the late emperor's charge.

sentences.zh: 時陛下亦侍先帝側。

translations.literal: Your Majesty was also attending the Late Emperor at his side."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty was standing at the late emperor's side that day."

sentences.zh: 」帝改容曰：「誠有斯旨。

translations.literal: The emperor changed expression and said, "There truly was such an intent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face softened. "That charge was indeed given," he said.

sentences.zh: 」於是舍之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he released him.
translations.idiomatic: He let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 數日，出為汶山太守。

translations.literal: Several days later he was sent out as Administrator of Wenshan.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Chun was posted out as administrator of Wenshan.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，突厥寇邊，轉榆林太守。

translations.literal: After a year the Turks raided the frontier; he was transferred to Administrator of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: A year on, when the Turks raided the frontier, he was moved to administrator of Yulin.

sentences.zh: 會彭城賊帥張大彪、宗世模等保懸薄山，帝令純討破之，斬萬餘級，築為京觀。

translations.literal: When the bandit chiefs of Pengcheng Zhang Dabiao, Zong Shimou and others held Xuanshan, the emperor ordered Chun to defeat them; more than ten thousand heads were struck off and piled into a victory mound.
translations.idiomatic: When the Pengcheng bandit chiefs Zhang Dabiao and Zong Shimou held Xuanshan, the emperor sent Chun against them; he cut down more than ten thousand and raised a victory mound of heads.

sentences.zh: 又破賊魏麒麟于單父。

translations.literal: He again defeated the bandit Wei Qilin at Shanfu.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the bandit Wei Qilin at Shanfu as well.

sentences.zh: 及帝重征遼東，復以純為彭城留守。

translations.literal: When the emperor again campaigned against Liaodong, Chun was again made garrison commander of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched on Liaodong again, Chun was again left to hold Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 東海賊彭孝才轉入沂水，保伍不及山，純擊之，禽孝才於陣，車裂之。

translations.literal: The bandit of Donghai Peng Xiaocai turned into Yi River and held Wu Buji Mountain; Chun attacked and took Xiaocai alive in battle, then had him torn apart by chariots.
translations.idiomatic: The Donghai bandit Peng Xiaocai crossed into the Yi and held Wu Buji Mountain; Chun struck him, took him alive in battle, and had him torn apart by chariots.

sentences.zh: 時盜賊日益，純雖克捷，而所在蜂起。

translations.literal: Bandits grew daily; though Chun won victories, troubles sprang up everywhere he was.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry swelled by the day; though Chun kept winning, new uprisings flared wherever he turned.

sentences.zh: 有譖純怯懦不能平賊，帝遣鎖詣東都。

translations.literal: Some slandered Chun as cowardly and unable to pacify bandits; the emperor sent him in chains to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Slanderers claimed Chun was too timid to crush the rebels; the emperor had him hauled to the eastern capital in chains.

sentences.zh: 有司見帝怒甚，希旨致純死罪，竟誅。

translations.literal: The ministry, seeing the emperor's rage, curried favor and imposed death on Chun; in the end he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The officials, reading the emperor's fury, bent the law to secure Chun's death; in the end he was executed.

sentences.zh: 魚俱羅，馮翊下邽人。

translations.literal: Yu Juluo was a native of Xiazhai in Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Juluo came from Xiazhai in Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，膂力絕人，聲氣雄壯，言聞數百步。

translations.literal: Eight chi tall, strength beyond ordinary men, voice and bearing martial and grand; his words were heard hundreds of paces away.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi tall, with strength beyond any ordinary man; his voice rang like a war drum and carried for hundreds of paces.

sentences.zh: 為大都督，從晉王廣平陳，以功拜開府。

translations.literal: As a grand colonel he followed Prince Jin Guang in pacifying Chen and for merit was made Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: As a grand colonel he followed Prince Guang of Jin against Chen and, for merit, was made a commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 及沈玄懀、高智慧等作亂江南，楊素以俱羅壯勇，請與同行。

translations.literal: When Shen Xuanyi, Gao Zhihui and others rebelled in the south, Yang Su because Juluo was mighty and brave asked that he march with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Xuanyi, Gao Zhihui, and others rebelled in the south, Yang Su asked to take the mighty Juluo with him.

sentences.zh: 有功，加上開府，封高唐縣公，拜疊州總管。

translations.literal: For merit he was raised to Upper Pillar of State, enfeoffed Duke of Gaotang county, and made Governor-General of Diezhou.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was made upper pillar of state, enfeoffed as duke of Gaotang county, and posted as governor-general of Diezhou.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 還至扶風，會楊素將出靈州道擊突厥，逢之，送與俱行。

translations.literal: Returning to Fufeng, he met Yang Su about to march out the Lingzhou route against the Turks; encountering him, Yang Su took him along.
translations.idiomatic: On his way back through Fufeng he met Yang Su setting out by the Lingzhou road against the Turks; Yang Su took him along.

sentences.zh: 及遇賊，俱羅與數騎奔擊，瞋目大呼，所當皆披靡。

translations.literal: When they met the enemy, Juluo with several horsemen charged; glaring and shouting, all before him gave way.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy appeared, Juluo charged with a handful of horsemen; glaring and roaring, he scattered everything in his path.

sentences.zh: 以功進位柱國，拜豐州總管。

translations.literal: For merit he advanced to Pillar of State and was made Governor-General of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was raised to pillar of state and made governor-general of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 突厥入境，輒禽斬之，自是屏跡，不敢畜牧於塞下。

translations.literal: Whenever Turks crossed the border he seized and beheaded them; thereafter they withdrew and dared not graze below the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Turks crossed the border he hunted them down and took their heads; after that they vanished from the frontier and dared not pasture below the passes.

sentences.zh: 初，煬帝在籓，俱羅弟贊以左右從，累遷大都督。

translations.literal: At first when Emperor Yang was still at his princely establishment, Juluo's younger brother Zan attended him as a personal guard and rose to grand colonel.
translations.idiomatic: While Yang Di was still heir, Juluo's younger brother Zan served in his personal guard and rose to grand colonel.

sentences.zh: 及帝嗣位，拜車騎將軍。

translations.literal: When the emperor succeeded, Zan was made General of the Grooms.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Di took the throne, Zan was made general of the grooms.

sentences.zh: 贊凶暴，令左右炙肉，遇不中意，以簽刺瞎其眼，溫酒不適口者，立斷其舌。

translations.literal: Zan was vicious and cruel; he had his attendants roast meat, and if it displeased him he stabbed out their eyes with an awl; if the warmed wine was not to his taste he at once cut out their tongues.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was savage and cruel; he made attendants roast meat for him, and if it displeased him he stabbed out their eyes with an awl; if the warmed wine was not to his taste he cut out their tongues on the spot.

sentences.zh: 帝以籓邸之舊，不忍加誅，謂近臣曰：「弟既如此，兄亦可知。

translations.literal: The emperor, because of old ties at the princely residence, could not bear to execute him; he told his close attendants, "If the younger brother is like this, the elder brother may be imagined."
translations.idiomatic: Because of old ties from the prince's household the emperor could not bring himself to execute Zan; he told his intimates, "If the younger brother is like this, you can guess what the elder is like."

sentences.zh: 」因召俱羅責之，出贊於獄，令自為計。

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned Juluo to rebuke him, released Zan from prison, and told him to settle his own affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Juluo to rebuke him, released Zan from prison, and told him to settle his own affairs.

sentences.zh: 贊至家，飲藥而死。

translations.literal: Zan reached home and drank poison to die.
translations.idiomatic: Zan went home and took poison.

sentences.zh: 帝恐俱羅不安，慮生邊患，轉安州刺史，遷趙郡太守。

translations.literal: The emperor feared Juluo would be unsettled and might breed frontier trouble; he transferred him to Administrator of Anzhou, then moved him to Administrator of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Juluo would turn restless and stir trouble on the frontier, the emperor moved him to Anzhou, then to administrator of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 後因朝集至東都，與將軍梁伯隱有舊，數相往來。

translations.literal: Later, coming to the eastern capital for the court assembly, he had old ties with General Liang Boyin and they often visited each other.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at the court assembly in the eastern capital, he renewed an old friendship with General Liang Boyin and they visited often.

sentences.zh: 又從郡多將雜物以貢獻，帝不受，因遺權貴。

translations.literal: From his commandery he also brought many mixed goods as tribute; the emperor would not accept them, so he gave them to powerful men at court.
translations.idiomatic: He also brought a train of curios from his commandery as tribute; when the emperor refused them, he passed them to men of influence at court.

sentences.zh: 御史劾俱羅以郡將交通內臣，帝大怒，與伯隱俱坐除名。

translations.literal: The censor impeached Juluo for a commandery general trafficking with inner attendants; the emperor was furious and both Juluo and Boyin were struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Censors charged Juluo with trafficking with palace eunuchs as a frontier commander; the emperor was furious and struck both Juluo and Boyin from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 未幾，越巂飛山蠻反，詔俱羅白衣領將，並率蜀郡都尉段鐘葵討平之。
