translations.literal: Before long the Feishan tribes of Yuexi rebelled; an edict had Juluo, in plain clothes, take command of troops, and together with the commandery colonel of Shu Duan Zhongkui he pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Feishan tribes of Yuexi rebelled; Juluo was ordered to take command in plain clothes, and with the Shu commandery colonel Duan Zhongkui he put them down.

sentences.zh: 大業九年，重征高麗，以俱羅為碣石道軍將。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daye, when Liaodong was again attacked, Juluo was made army commander of the Jieshi route.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Daye, during the renewed Liaodong campaign, Juluo was made army commander on the Jieshi route.

sentences.zh: 及還，江南劉元進作亂，詔俱羅將兵向會稽諸郡逐捕之。

translations.literal: On the return, Liu Yuanjin rebelled in Jiangnan; an edict ordered Juluo to lead troops through the Kuaiji commanderies in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: On the withdrawal Liu Yuanjin rose in Jiangnan; an edict sent Juluo with troops through the Kuaiji commanderies to hunt him down.

sentences.zh: 時百姓思亂，從盜如市，俱羅擊賊帥硃燮、管崇等，戰無不捷。

translations.literal: The people longed for rebellion and joined bandits like a market; Juluo struck the bandit chiefs Zhu Xie, Guan Chong and others and was never defeated in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The people were ripe for revolt and flocked to the bandits like buyers at a market; Juluo struck the chiefs Zhu Xie and Guan Chong and never lost a fight.

sentences.zh: 然賊勢浸盛，敗而復聚。

translations.literal: Yet the bandits' power grew daily; beaten, they regathered.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the rebels grew stronger by the day; beaten once, they gathered again.

sentences.zh: 俱羅度賊非歲月可平，諸子並在京、洛，又見天下漸亂，終恐道路隔絕。

translations.literal: Juluo judged the bandits could not be pacified in months; his sons were all in the capital; he also saw the realm slipping into chaos and feared the roads would be cut.
translations.idiomatic: Juluo saw the rebels could not be crushed in a season; his sons were all in the capital, and with the empire sliding into chaos he feared the roads would close.

sentences.zh: 于時東都饑饉，穀食踴貴，俱羅遣家僮將船米至東都糶之，益市財貨，潛迎諸子。

translations.literal: At that time the eastern capital was famine-stricken; grain leaped in price; Juluo sent household slaves with boats of rice to sell grain in the eastern capital, bought more goods, and secretly brought in his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Famine gripped the eastern capital and grain soared in price; Juluo sent household slaves with boatloads of rice to sell there, bought goods, and quietly brought his sons in.

sentences.zh: 朝廷微知之，恐有異志，案驗不得其罪。

translations.literal: The court came slightly to know this and feared he harbored other intent; investigation could not fix a crime on him.
translations.idiomatic: The court caught wind of this and suspected disloyalty, but investigation could not pin a crime on him.

sentences.zh: 帝復令大理司直梁敬真就鎖將詣東都，俱羅相表異人，目有重瞳，陰為帝之所忌。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent the director of the Court for Trial Liang Jingzhen to go in chains to the eastern capital; Juluo had an unusual countenance and double pupils in his eyes—secretly what the emperor dreaded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Liang Jingzhen of the court for trial to fetch him in chains to the eastern capital; Juluo had a strange face and double pupils in his eyes—traits the emperor secretly dreaded.

sentences.zh: 敬真希旨，奏俱羅師徒敗衄，斬東都市，家口籍沒。

translations.literal: Jingzhen curried favor and memorialized that Juluo's army had been routed; he was beheaded in the eastern capital market and his household was registered for confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen played to the emperor's mood and reported that Juluo's army had been routed; Juluo was beheaded in the eastern capital market and his household was seized.

sentences.zh: 王辯，字警略，馮翊蒲城人也。

translations.literal: Wang Bian, styled Jinglüe, was a native of Pucheng in Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bian, courtesy name Jinglüe, came from Pucheng in Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 祖訓，以行商致富。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xun grew rich as a traveling merchant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xun made a fortune as an itinerant merchant.

sentences.zh: 魏世，出粟助給軍糧，為假清河太守。

translations.literal: In Wei times he released grain to supply the army and was made acting Administrator of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei he donated grain to feed the armies and was made acting administrator of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 辯少習兵書，尤善騎射，慷慨有大志。

translations.literal: Bian in youth studied military books and was especially skilled at mounted archery; he was ardent and had great ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Bian studied the military classics in youth and excelled at mounted archery; he was bold and burned with ambition.

sentences.zh: 在周，以軍功授帥都督。

translations.literal: Under Zhou, for military merit he was given the office of Commander-in-Chief of a Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he earned the post of garrison commander for military merit.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，累遷車騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era he rose repeatedly to General of the Grooms.
translations.idiomatic: In the Renshou era he rose step by step to general of the grooms.

sentences.zh: 後從楊素討平漢王諒，賜爵武寧縣男。

translations.literal: Later, following Yang Su in putting down Prince of Han Liang, he was granted the peerage of Baron of Wuning county.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Yang Su against Prince Liang of Han and was ennobled as baron of Wuning county.

sentences.zh: 累以軍功，加至通議大夫，尋遷武賁郎將。

translations.literal: Repeatedly for military merit he rose to Master for Comprehensive Discussion, and soon after was made Bold Tiger Guard Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated victories raised him to master for comprehensive discussion, and soon after to bold tiger guard commandant.

sentences.zh: 及山東盜賊起，帝引辯升禦榻，問以方略。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Shandong, the emperor drew Bian up to the imperial couch and asked his strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When banditry flared in Shandong, the emperor had Bian sit beside him on the couch and asked his plan.

sentences.zh: 辯論取賊勢，帝稱善曰：「誠如此，賊不足憂。

translations.literal: Bian analyzed the bandits' strength; the emperor praised him and said, "If it is truly so, the bandits are nothing to fear."
translations.idiomatic: Bian laid out the rebels' strength; the emperor praised him and said, "If that is so, the bandits are nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 」於是發從行步騎三千，擊敗之，賜黃金二百兩。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was sent with three thousand infantry and cavalry in attendance; he defeated them and was given two hundred taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out with three thousand foot and horse; he routed the bandits and was rewarded with two hundred taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 勃海賊帥高士達自號東海公，眾以萬數。

translations.literal: The Bohai bandit chief Gao Shida styled himself Duke of the Eastern Sea; his followers numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shida, a bandit chief in Bohai, called himself Duke of the Eastern Sea, and his host ran to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 令辯擊之，屢挫其銳。

translations.literal: Bian was ordered to attack him and repeatedly blunted their edge.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was sent against him and again and again broke their spearhead.

sentences.zh: 帝在江都宮，聞而召之，及見，禮賜甚厚，復令往信都經略士達，復戰破之，優詔褒顯。

translations.literal: The emperor was at Jiangdu Palace; on hearing of it he summoned him; when they met, gifts and courtesy were lavish; he again sent him to Xindu to deal with Shida; he again defeated him in battle, and an edict of special praise was issued.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was at Jiangdu Palace; when he heard, he called Bian in. At the audience gifts and courtesy were lavish. He sent him back to Xindu to deal with Shida; Bian beat him again, and the court issued a warm edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 時賊帥郝孝德、孫宣雅、時季康、竇建德、魏刀兒等往往屯聚，大者十數萬，小者數千，寇掠河北。

translations.literal: At that time the bandit chiefs Hao Xiaode, Sun Xuanya, Shi Jikang, Dou Jiande, Wei Dao'er, and others were constantly gathering—large bands a hundred thousand strong, small ones a few thousand—plundering Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit chiefs Hao Xiaode, Sun Xuanya, Shi Jikang, Dou Jiande, Wei Dao'er, and others were camped all over the land, some with a hundred thousand men, some with only a few thousand, raiding Hebei.

sentences.zh: 辯擊之，所向皆捷。

translations.literal: Bian attacked them; wherever he turned, he won.
translations.idiomatic: Bian struck them wherever he marched and always won.

sentences.zh: 及翟讓寇徐、豫，辯頻擊走之。

translations.literal: When Zhai Rang raided Xu and Yu, Bian repeatedly drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhai Rang raided Xu and Yu, Bian drove him off again and again.

sentences.zh: 讓尋與李密屯據洛口倉，辯與王世充討密，阻洛水相持經年。

translations.literal: Rang soon joined Li Mi in holding the Luokou granary; Bian and Wang Shichong campaigned against Mi, facing each other across the Luo River for more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: Rang soon joined Li Mi in seizing the Luokou granary. Bian and Wang Shichong campaigned against Mi and faced each other across the Luo for more than a year.

sentences.zh: 辯攻敗密。

translations.literal: Bian attacked and defeated Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Bian attacked and broke Mi.

sentences.zh: 乘勝將入城，世充不知，恐將士勞倦，鳴角收兵，翻為密徒所乘，官軍大潰，不可救止。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory he was about to enter the city; Shichong did not know, fearing his troops were weary, sounded the horn to withdraw; the enemy seized the chance and the government army collapsed in great rout beyond saving.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was pressing the victory and about to enter the city. Shichong, not knowing, feared his men were spent and sounded the horn to recall them. Mi's troops seized the moment; the imperial army broke in a rout that could not be stopped.

sentences.zh: 辯至洛水，橋已壞。

translations.literal: Bian reached the Luo River; the bridge was already broken.
translations.idiomatic: Bian reached the Luo; the bridge was already gone.

sentences.zh: 遂涉水至中流，為溺人所引墜馬，竟溺死。

translations.literal: He forded the water to midstream; drowning men grabbed and pulled him from his horse, and he drowned at last.
translations.idiomatic: He waded in to midstream; men in the water caught and dragged him from his horse, and he drowned.

sentences.zh: 三軍莫不痛惜之。

translations.literal: All three armies grieved for him without exception.
translations.idiomatic: The whole army mourned him.

sentences.zh: 時有河南斛斯萬善，驍勇果毅，與辯齊名。

translations.literal: At the time there was the Henan man Husi Wanshan, fierce and resolute, famed alongside Bian.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Husi Wanshan of Henan was fierce and bold, with a name to match Bian's.

sentences.zh: 從衛玄討楊玄感，萬善與數騎追及之，玄感窘迫自殺。

translations.literal: Following Wei Xuan against Yang Xuangan, Wanshan with a few riders overtook him; Xuangan, hard pressed, killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Yang Xuangan under Wei Xuan, Wanshan with a few riders ran him down; Xuangan, cornered, killed himself.

sentences.zh: 由是知名，拜武賁郎將。

translations.literal: Thereby he became known and was made bold tiger guard commandant.
translations.idiomatic: From that he won a name and was made bold tiger guard commandant.

sentences.zh: 突厥始畢之圍雁門，萬善奮擊之，所向皆破。

translations.literal: When the Shibi Qaghan of the Turks besieged Yanmen, Wanshan fought bravely against them; wherever he turned, he broke them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shibi qaghan of the Turks besieged Yanmen, Wanshan struck hard; wherever he turned, the enemy broke.

sentences.zh: 由是突厥莫敢逼城，十許日竟退，萬善力也。

translations.literal: Thereby the Turks did not dare press the walls; in a little more than ten days they withdrew at last—Wanshan's doing.
translations.idiomatic: After that the Turks did not dare press the walls. In a little more than ten days they drew off at last, and it was Wanshan's work.

sentences.zh: 後頻討群盜，累功至將軍。

translations.literal: Later he repeatedly campaigned against bandit gangs and through cumulative merit rose to general.
translations.idiomatic: Later he campaigned again and again against bandits and by piled merit rose to general.

sentences.zh: 又有將軍鹿願、范貴、馮孝慈，俱為將帥，數從征伐，並有名於世。

translations.literal: There were also the generals Lu Yuan, Fan Gui, and Feng Xiaoci—all were commanders, repeatedly followed campaigns, and all had names in the world.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the generals Lu Yuan, Fan Gui, and Feng Xiaoci, all field commanders who followed many campaigns and all had names in their day.

sentences.zh: 事皆亡失，故史官闕云。

translations.literal: Their deeds are all lost; therefore the historians leave them unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: Their deeds are lost, and the historians pass them by in silence.

sentences.zh: 陳稜，字長威，廬江襄安人也。

translations.literal: Chen Ling, styled Changwei, was a native of Xiang'an in Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ling, courtesy name Changwei, came from Xiang'an in Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 祖碩，以漁釣自給。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shuo supported himself by fishing.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shuo lived by fishing.

sentences.zh: 父峴，少驍勇，事章大寶為帳內部曲。

translations.literal: His father Xian in youth was fierce and brave and served Zhang Dabao as a personal guard in the headquarters retinue.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xian was fierce and brave in youth and served Zhang Dabao as a guard in his personal retinue.

sentences.zh: 告大寶反，授譙州刺史。

translations.literal: He reported Dabao's rebellion and was made governor of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: He denounced Dabao for rebellion and was made governor of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 陳滅，廢於家。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, he was dismissed and lived at home.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, he was stripped of office and lived at home.

sentences.zh: 高智慧、汪文進反，廬江豪傑亦舉兵相應。

translations.literal: Gao Zhihui and Wang Wenjin rebelled; the Lujiang magnates also raised troops in response.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhihui and Wang Wenjin rose in revolt, and the great families of Lujiang also took up arms in answer.

sentences.zh: 以峴舊將，共推為主。

translations.literal: Because Xian was an old commander, they together made him their leader.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xian was a veteran commander, they together pushed him to lead them.

sentences.zh: 峴欲拒之，稜謂峴曰：「眾亂既作，拒之禍且及己，不如偽從，別為後計。

translations.literal: Xian wished to refuse; Ling said to Xian: "The crowd is already in revolt; to refuse will bring disaster on yourself—better to feign compliance and plan afterward."
translations.idiomatic: Xian wanted to refuse. Ling told him, "The mob is already in arms. Refuse and the harm will reach you. Better to pretend to go along and plan another way."

sentences.zh: 」峴然之。

translations.literal: Xian agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Xian agreed.

sentences.zh: 後潛使稜至柱國李徹所，請為內應。

translations.literal: Later he secretly sent Ling to the pillar of state Li Che to ask to serve as an inside contact.
translations.idiomatic: Later he secretly sent Ling to the pillar of state Li Che to offer himself as an inside man.

sentences.zh: 徹上其事，拜上大將軍、宣州刺史，封譙郡公，詔徹應接之。

translations.literal: Che reported the matter upward; Ling was made upper grand general and governor of Xuan, enfeoffed as Duke of Qiao commandery, and an edict ordered Che to link up with him.
translations.idiomatic: Che sent up the report. Ling was made upper grand general and governor of Xuan, enfeoffed as duke of Qiao commandery, and the court ordered Che to join with him.

sentences.zh: 徹軍未至，謀泄，為其黨所殺，稜以獲免。

translations.literal: Che's army had not yet arrived when the plot leaked; Xian was killed by his own faction, and Ling escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Che's army had not yet come when the plot leaked. The rebels killed Xian, but Ling was spared.

sentences.zh: 上以其父之故，拜開府，尋領鄉兵。

translations.literal: The emperor, because of his father, made him a grand opening and soon put him in charge of local militia.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, for his father's sake, made him a grand opening and soon set him over local militia.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，拜武賁郎將。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye he was made bold tiger guard commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daye he was made bold tiger guard commandant.

sentences.zh: 後與朝請大夫張鎮周自義安泛海擊流求國，月餘而至。

translations.literal: Later, with the court gentleman Zhang Zhenzhou, he crossed the sea from Yi'an to attack the kingdom of Liuqiu; after more than a month they arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and the court gentleman Zhang Zhenzhou sailed from Yi'an across the sea against Liuqiu and came to land after more than a month.

sentences.zh: 流求人初見船艦，以為商旅，往往詣軍貿易。

translations.literal: When the Liuqiu people first saw the ships, they took them for merchants and often came to the army to trade.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liuqiu people first saw the fleet, they took it for merchant traffic and often came to the camp to trade.

sentences.zh: 稜率眾登岸，遣鎮周為先鋒。

translations.literal: Ling led the host ashore and sent Zhenzhou as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Ling led his men ashore and sent Zhenzhou ahead as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 其主歡斯渴刺兜遣兵拒戰，鎮周頻破之。

translations.literal: Their ruler Huansikoucidou sent troops to resist; Zhenzhou repeatedly broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Their king Huansikoucidou sent troops to meet them; Zhenzhou beat them again and again.

sentences.zh: 稜進至低沒檀洞，其小王歡斯老模拒戰，稜敗之，斬老模。

translations.literal: Ling advanced to the cave of Dimotan; the lesser king Huansilaomo resisted; Ling defeated him and beheaded Laomo.
translations.idiomatic: Ling pushed on to the cave of Dimotan. The lesser king Huansilaomo fought him; Ling broke him and took Laomo's head.

sentences.zh: 其日霧雨晦冥，將士皆懼，稜刑白馬以祭海神，既而開霽。

translations.literal: That day fog and rain made the sky dark; officers and soldiers were all afraid; Ling executed a white horse to sacrifice to the sea god, and soon the weather cleared.
translations.idiomatic: That day fog and rain shut out the sky and the troops were afraid. Ling sacrificed a white horse to the sea god, and the weather cleared.

sentences.zh: 分為五軍，趣其都邑，乘勝逐北，至其柵，破之，斬渴刺兜，獲其子島槌，虜男女數千而歸。

translations.literal: He divided into five armies, hurried on their capital, pressed the victory northward to their palisade, broke it, beheaded Koucidou, captured his son Daozhui, and returned with several thousand men and women as captives.
translations.idiomatic: He split into five columns, rushed their capital, chased the rout to their stockade, broke it, killed Koucidou, took his son Daozhui, and came back with several thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 加稜右光祿大夫，鎮周金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Ling was advanced to right grand master for splendid happiness; Zhenzhou was made grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Ling was raised to right grand master for splendid happiness; Zhenzhou was made grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，以宿衛遷左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign, through palace guard service he was moved to left grand master for splendid happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong war he was moved, for palace guard service, to left grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝復征遼東，稜為東萊留守。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor again campaigned against Liaodong; Ling was left to guard Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor marched on Liaodong again, and Ling was left as guardian of Donglai.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感反，稜擊平黎陽，斬玄感所署刺史元務本。

translations.literal: Yang Xuangan rebelled; Ling attacked and pacified Liyang and beheaded Xuangan's appointed governor Yuan Wuben.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuangan rebelled. Ling crushed Liyang and beheaded Yuan Wuben, whom Xuangan had set over the district.

sentences.zh: 尋奉詔于江南營戰艦。

translations.literal: Soon he received an edict to build war vessels in the lower Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to build warships in the lower Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 至彭城，賊帥孟讓據都梁宮，阻淮為固。

translations.literal: Reaching Pengcheng, the bandit chief Meng Rang held the Duliang Palace and blocked the Huai as a stronghold.
translations.idiomatic: At Pengcheng the bandit Meng Rang held the Duliang Palace and made the Huai his wall.

sentences.zh: 稜潛於下流而濟，至江都，襲破讓。

translations.literal: Ling crossed secretly downstream, reached Jiangdu, and struck and broke Rang.
translations.idiomatic: Ling crossed downstream by stealth, reached Jiangdu, and smashed Rang.

sentences.zh: 以功進位光祿大夫，賜爵信安侯。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced to grand master of the palace and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was raised to grand master of the palace and enfeoffed as marquis of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 後帝幸江都宮，俄而李子通據海陵，左才相掠淮北，杜伏威屯六合，帝遣厣夌擊之，往見克捷，超拜右禦衛將軍。

translations.literal: Later the emperor visited Jiangdu Palace; soon Li Zitong held Hailing, Zuo Caixiang plundered north of the Huai, and Du Fuwei camped at Liuhe; the emperor sent Ling to attack them; he went and won at once and was promoted to right imperial guard general.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor went to Jiangdu Palace. Li Zitong seized Hailing, Zuo Caixiang raided north of the Huai, and Du Fuwei held Liuhe. The emperor sent Ling against them; he went, won at once, and was jumped to right imperial guard general.

sentences.zh: 復度清江，擊宣城賊。

translations.literal: He again crossed the Qing River and attacked the bandits of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Qing River again and struck the Xuancheng bandits.

sentences.zh: 俄而帝以弑崩，宇文化及引軍北上，召稜守江都。

translations.literal: Soon the emperor died by assassination; Yuwen Huaji led his army north and summoned Ling to hold Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor was murdered. Yuwen Huaji marched north and called Ling to guard Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 稜集眾縞素，為煬帝發喪，備儀衛，改葬于吳公台下，衰杖送喪，慟感行路，論者深義之。

translations.literal: Ling gathered the crowd in white mourning, held funeral rites for Emperor Yang, prepared full ceremonial guard, and reburied him below the Terrace of Duke Wu; with mourning staff they escorted the coffin, moving passersby to grief; commentators deeply praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Ling called the troops out in white, gave Yang Di a full funeral, set out the guard of honor, and reburied him below the Terrace of Duke Wu. They escorted the coffin with mourning staffs, and travelers on the road wept. Men of judgment praised his sense of duty.

sentences.zh: 稜後為李子通所陷，奔杜伏威，伏威忌而害之。

translations.literal: Later Ling was trapped by Li Zitong, fled to Du Fuwei, and Fuwei, jealous, killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ling was undone by Li Zitong, fled to Du Fuwei, and Fuwei, envying him, put him to death.

sentences.zh: 十二年，帝將幸江都，才見四海土崩，諫請還京師，安兆庶。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, as the emperor was about to visit Jiangdu, Cai saw that the four seas were collapsing and admonished him to return to the capital and reassure the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, as the emperor was about to go to Jiangdu, Cai saw the realm breaking apart and urged him to return to the capital and steady the people.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，以才屬吏，旬日乃出之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, handed Cai over to the law officers, and only after ten days released him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, handed Cai to the law officers, and only let him out after ten days.

sentences.zh: 遂幸江都，待遇逾昵。

translations.literal: He then went to Jiangdu, and Cai's treatment grew ever more intimate.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Jiangdu all the same, and favored Cai more than ever.

sentences.zh: 時江都糧盡，內史侍郎虞世基、秘書監袁充等多勸帝幸丹陽。

translations.literal: At that time Jiangdu was out of grain; the vice director of the Secretariat Yu Shiji, the director of the Library Yuan Chong, and many others urged the emperor to go to Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Grain at Jiangdu was gone. Yu Shiji, vice director of the secretariat, Yuan Chong, director of the library, and many others urged the emperor to move to Danyang.

sentences.zh: 才極陳入京策，世基極言度江便。

translations.literal: Cai argued the plan to enter the capital with all his force; Shiji argued just as hard that crossing the river was best.
translations.idiomatic: Cai pressed the plan to return to the capital with all his might; Shiji pressed just as hard that crossing the Yangtze was better.

sentences.zh: 帝無言，才與世基相忿而出。

translations.literal: The emperor said nothing; Cai and Shiji left in mutual anger.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing. Cai and Shiji stalked out, furious with each other.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及殺逆之際，才時在苑北，化及遣驍果席德方執之，謂曰：「今日之事，祇得如此。

translations.literal: At the time of Yuwen Huaji's regicide, Cai was in the north of the park; Huaji sent the elite guard Xi Defang to seize him and said: "Today's affair can only be thus."
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji murdered the emperor, Cai was in the north park. Huaji sent the elite guard Xi Defang to seize him and said, "What is done today could only be done this way."

sentences.zh: 」才默然不對。

translations.literal: Cai was silent and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Cai said nothing.

sentences.zh: 化及忿才無言，將殺之，三日乃釋，以本官從事，鬱鬱不得志。

translations.literal: Huaji, angry that Cai would not speak, was about to kill him; after three days he released him and kept him in his former office; Cai was depressed and could not find his will.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji, furious at Cai's silence, was about to kill him, but after three days let him go and kept him at his old post. Cai brooded and could not settle his mind.

sentences.zh: 才嘗對化及宴，請勸其同謀逆者十八人楊士覽等酒，化及許之。

translations.literal: Cai once at a feast with Huaji asked leave to pour wine for the eighteen men who had joined the plot, including Yang Shilan; Huaji agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a feast with Huaji, Cai asked to pour wine for the eighteen men who had joined the plot, Yang Shilan among them. Huaji agreed.

sentences.zh: 才執杯曰：「十八人止可一度作，勿復餘處更為。

translations.literal: Cai took up the cup and said: "The eighteen may do this only once; do not do it again elsewhere."
translations.idiomatic: Cai raised his cup and said, "You eighteen may do this once only. Do not do it again anywhere else."

sentences.zh: 諸人默然不對。

translations.literal: The men were silent and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The men said nothing.

sentences.zh: 行止聊城，遇疾。

translations.literal: On the march they stopped at Liaocheng; he fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: On the road they halted at Liaocheng, and he fell ill.

sentences.zh: 俄而化及為竇建德所破，才復見虜。

translations.literal: Soon Huaji was broken by Dou Jiande, and Cai was captured again.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Huaji was broken by Dou Jiande, and Cai was taken again.

sentences.zh: 心彌不平，數日而卒。

translations.literal: His heart grew ever more bitter; within days he died.
translations.idiomatic: His heart would not quiet; within days he was dead.

sentences.zh: 仁壽、大業間有蘭興洛、賀蘭蕃，俱為武候將軍，剛嚴正直，不避強禦，咸以稱職知名。

translations.literal: Between Renshou and Daye there were Lan Xingluo and Helan Fan, both martial guard generals, stern and upright, not shrinking from the powerful, and all were known for fulfilling their duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the Renshou and Daye eras Lan Xingluo and Helan Fan served as martial guard generals, hard and upright, unafraid of the powerful, and both won names for doing their duty.

sentences.zh: 論曰：虎嘯風生，龍騰雲起，英賢奪發，亦各因時。

translations.literal: The commentators say: When the tiger roars, the wind rises; when the dragon soars, clouds gather; heroes and worthies break forth, each in his season.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: When the tiger roars, wind rises; when the dragon soars, clouds gather. Heroes break out, each in his time.

sentences.zh: 張定和、張ＣＯ、麥鐵杖皆一時壯士，而困於貧賤。

translations.literal: Zhang Dinghe, Zhang Ben, and Mai Tiezhang were all warriors of an age, yet trapped in poverty and low status.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dinghe, Zhang Ben, and Mai Tiezhang were all fierce men of their day, yet they languished in poverty.

sentences.zh: 當其鬱抑未遇，亦安知有鴻鵠志哉！

translations.literal: When they were depressed and had not yet met their chance, how could they have known the ambition of the great swan!
translations.idiomatic: When they were still obscure, who could have guessed they harbored the swan's ambition?

sentences.zh: 終能振拔汙泥，申其力用，符馬革之願，快生平之必，得丈夫之節矣。

translations.literal: In the end they could shake off the mud, show their strength, match the vow of the horse-hide shroud, fulfill the ardor of a lifetime, and win a true man's constancy.
translations.idiomatic: In the end they shook off the mud, used their strength, kept the vow to die wrapped in horsehide, tasted the fulfillment of a life spent hard, and won a true man's honor.

sentences.zh: 孟才、錢傑、沈光等感懷恩舊，臨難亡身，雖功無所成，其志有可稱矣。

translations.literal: Mengcai, Qian Jie, Shen Guang, and the rest were moved by old grace; facing death they gave their lives; though their deeds won nothing, their will is worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Mengcai, Qian Jie, Shen Guang, and the rest remembered old favor and gave their lives in crisis. Their deeds came to nothing, yet their will deserves praise.

sentences.zh: 權武素無行檢，不拘刑憲，終取黜辱，不亦宜哉！

translations.literal: Quan Wu by nature had no restraint, did not bow to law and punishment, and in the end met disgrace and ruin—is this not fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Quan Wu had never kept his conduct in check or bowed to the law, and in the end met disgrace. Was that not fitting?

sentences.zh: 仁恭武毅見知，文以取達，初在汲郡，清能可紀，後居馬邑，貪吝而亡。

translations.literal: Rengong was known for martial sternness; he rose through literary skill; at first in Ji commandery his clean ability could be recorded; later at Mayi he was greedy and stingy and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong was known for martial grit and rose by polish in letters. In Ji commandery at first his clean rule was worth recording; at Mayi later he turned greedy and died for it.

sentences.zh: 鮮克有終，斯言乃驗。

translations.literal: Few can keep the end; this saying was proved true.
translations.idiomatic: Few men finish well; the old saying held true.

sentences.zh: 吐萬緒、董純以萑蒲不翦，遽嬰罪戮。

translations.literal: Tuwu Xu and Dong Chun, because the thorns and rushes were not cut, suddenly met punishment and execution.
translations.idiomatic: Tuwu Xu and Dong Chun, because the weeds were never cleared, suddenly met the axe.

sentences.zh: 大業之季，盜可盡乎？

translations.literal: In the last years of Daye, could bandits ever be exhausted?
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of Daye, could rebels ever be wiped out?

sentences.zh: 俱羅欲加之罪，非其咎釁。

translations.literal: Juluo's wish to attach guilt was not his true fault.
translations.idiomatic: When Juluo was destroyed, the charge laid on him was not his true crime.

sentences.zh: 王辯殞身勍敵，志在勤王。

translations.literal: Wang Bian died facing a fierce foe; his will was to serve the dynasty in earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bian fell before a fierce enemy with his heart set on saving the throne.

sentences.zh: 陳稜縞素髮喪，哀感行路，義之所動，固已深乎！

translations.literal: Chen Ling in white mourning raised the funeral; grief moved travelers on the road; what righteousness moves can indeed run deep!
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ling went out in white and gave the emperor a funeral that moved every traveler on the road. When righteousness stirs a man, it runs deep.

sentences.zh: 趙才雖人而無儀，志在強直，拒世基之諂，可謂不苟同矣。

translations.literal: Zhao Cai, though a man without ceremony, had a will set on firm uprightness; he rejected Shiji's flattery—one may call this refusing to go along.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Cai lacked polish, but his will was straight. He refused Shiji's flattery. That was a man who would not truckle.
